question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. What are the dimensions of the eigenspaces ${V}_{-2}$ and ${V}_{1}$ corresponding to eigenvalues $\lambda =-2$ and $\lambda =1$ of $A$, respectively?
question.worked_solution:
First, since the given matrix is triangular, its eigenvalues are the entries on the main diagonal. Hence, ${\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=1$ (double root) and ${\lambda }_{3}=-2$ (simple root).

Let's now consider the eigenspaces corresponding to each eigenvector:

- First, we consider $\lambda =-2.$ Since ${V}_{-2}$ correspond to a simple root, we obtain 

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{-2})=1.
$$

- Next, we consider $\lambda =1,$ which is a repeated root of the characteristic equation. To find the dimension of ${V}_{1},$ we row-reduce the matrix $(A-1I)\text{x}=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]-1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). This implies that we will have only $3-2=1$ linearly independent eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =1.$ Therefore, 

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{1})=1.
$$
